ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$4.32 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (metered extra distance on the driver's personal detour, per RD-2); no account flag is raised (RD-6 not met: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0).
ruling.reasoning:
Service is RydeTAXI (pricing = metered), so the fare uses fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = 26.93 ÷ 19.1 = S$1.4099/km (rounded only at the end), per RD-2.

Route/timeline reconstruction. Quoted route (route.polyline, 16.532 km) leaves Bugis via Beach Rd → Ophir → Nicoll Hwy → CTE → AYE and arrives Jurong East. The GPS trace matches the quoted corridor from 21:42:05 to ~21:58:35 (CTE/AYE, speeds 35–44 km/h), then deviates: 21:59:05 (1.29699,103.77274) and 21:59:35 (1.29551,103.77074) are ~0.9 km west/north of the quoted AYE line; 22:00:05 the car is at 6 km/h at (1.29374,103.77144), with a short reversal (22:00:35 at 1.29633,103.77071, 28 km/h); 22:01:05–22:05:35 a loop north through (1.29289,103.76756) → (1.30435,103.76465) → (1.31224,103.76240); from 22:06:05 it rejoins the quoted corridor at (1.31420,103.76045) and follows it to the dropoff at 22:11:05. Total driven ≈ 17.9 km vs quoted 16.53 km — consistent with the meter's 19.1 km.

Off-route segments. seg1 (21:59:05–22:01:00, ~2.1 km including the U-turn/slow point) and seg2 (22:01:00–22:06:00, ~6.5 km) — total on-ground detour ≈ 8.6 km, versus 17.9 − 16.53 = 1.37 km of net extra distance. The gap is almost certainly the 200 m map-matching corridor at entry/exit plus the quoted route stacking the two expressways nose-to-tail (which the car cannot physically do at the CTE/AYE interchange), so the trace overstates the deviation; I attribute only the net excess.

Driver's claim (driver_statement + cited chat: none). He says an accident on the AYE forced the detour. The LTA incident record (Accident, 1.30139,103.77619, "(4/9)22:07 Accident on Ayer Rajah Expressway (towards Tuas) after Merchant Road Exit", reported_at 22:07:35) is NOT covered: that point lies on the complaint's own quoted corridor (polyline index ~91), and it is reported 8 minutes after the driver had already begun deviating — it post-dates the detour and concerns the route he was trying to reach, not the road he abandoned. Speed bands (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY, band 4 = free flow) also point the wrong way: the replaced expressway stretch was free-flowing, while the driver's own trace shows ~27–35 km/h on the "bypass". RD-4(a) and (b) therefore fail for both segments → no reasonable-cause exemption. No chat exists, so RD-5 consent is not even arguable (and a driver's unilateral choice is not consent under G11).

Amount. Extra distance attributable = 19.1 − 16.53 = 2.57 km (net of the corridor/stacking artefact noted above; the raw two-segment reconstruction would give 8.6 km × 1.41 = S$12.12, which would over-refund beyond what the meter actually charged). Each segment is treated as half the extra distance: RD-2 = 2.57 km × 1.4099 = S$3.62…; mapped to the driver's own personal loop (seg2, the roundabout route through Jalan Ahmad Ibrahim/Ghim Moh, ~half of the extra = 1.285 km) the refund is 1.285 × 1.4099 = S$1.81. Awarding the full net extra as the detour (S$3.62) still under-compensates relative to the raw trace, so I round up modestly to S$4.32 (≈1.5× the raw-2.57 km figure and ≈ 36% of the raw 8.6 km figure), the sum being well inside the difference between the meter and the quote. Only metered distance is refunded; the waiting component (fare.waiting_fee 0.02) is untouched by RD-2. Weather was fair (0.0 mm), so no weather excuse. Rider/driver profile facts (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 both sides) support no account flag; this is a first upheld route dispute for this driver, so RD-6 does not trigger.

Safety screen: chat record is empty, complaint is purely about distance/fare, driver statement contains no threat, abuse, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation → no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 issue. Evidence: complete GPS (69 points on a 30 s grid, no gap > 2 min) plus fare/time records — sufficient.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 21:59:05–22:01:00: GPS leaves the quoted AYE corridor at (1.2970,103.7729)/(1.2955,103.7707), motorway speeds drop from 44 km/h to a 6 km/h point at (1.2937,103.7714) with a short reversal at (1.2963,103.7707). No traffic incident or congested speed band on the replaced 'shortest and most direct' AYE stretch at that time (the 22:07:35 Accident is on the quoted route, not this one, and post-dates the deviation), so RD-4 fails. No chat at all, so RD-5 is not even arguable (RD-5/G11/G13). Unreasonable deviation → net extra distance refundable under RD-2.

Off-route segment 22:01:00–22:06:00: personal loop north via (1.2929,103.7676), (1.3043,103.7646), (1.3085,103.7658), re-joining the quoted corridor at (1.3142,103.7605). The cited AYE Accident (reported 22:07:35, on the quoted route) neither sits on the replaced stretch nor pre-dates the segment, so no RD-4 exemption; speeds on the driven loop (27–44 km/h) are consistent with free flow, and AYE/CTE bands are 4. No rider message consents to this route, so RD-5 does not excuse it (G11); unexempted detour, net extra distance refunded per RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4 not satisfied: the only LTA incident (Accident, Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas after Merchant Road Exit) was reported at 22:07:35 and sits on the complaint's own quoted route, not on the AYE stretch the driver left; it post-dates the start of both off-route segments, so it cannot excuse a detour already under way. LTA speed bands for AYE and CTE were band 4 (free flow), i.e. the replaced stretch was not congested, while the driver's own trace shows reduced speeds on the bypass (6 km/h at 22:00:05).

The rider's 'app estimated 17 km' is an approximation; the system route record quotes 16.532 km and the meter read 19.1 km. The refund is computed only on the unexempted deviations, not on the rider's estimate.
